Timber is grown, harvested, and milled Principle 2: The logs are trucked, floated, or carried on railroads to asawmill (p. 14).
Timber is grown, harvested, and milled Principle 3: At the mill, logs are debarked (their bark is removed), and saws cut them into boards (lumber) (p. 14).
Timber is grown, harvested, and milled Principle 4: Small logs are often cut into boards in a single pass through a set of saws (a gang saw) that makes many cuts at once (p. 14).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Timber is grown, harvested, and milled): Largelogs may make several passes through one saw (a headsaw) thatslices off a board at a time until the whole log is cut into lumber (p. 14).
Step 2 (Timber is grown, harvested, and milled): The new lumber, called green lumber, is edged and trimmed tostraighten the sides and cut into boards of standard lengths (p. 14).
Step 3 (Timber is grown, harvested, and milled): Lumber is graded for quality, appearance, and strength (p. 14).
Step 4 (Timber is grown, harvested, and milled): Manufacturersuse them tomake flooring, pallets, andsimilar products (p. 14).
